chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Two rak'at that a married person prays are superior to seventy rak'at that an unmarried person prays.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward comparison between a married and unmarried person's prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to underscore the spiritual elevation of marriage, a cornerstone of Shia social ethics. The comparison of two rak'ahs to seventy highlights that the marital state, with its responsibilities and companionship, serves as a potent catalyst for increased divine reward and spiritual maturity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Hassan b. Ali from Ja’far b. Muhammad b. Hakeem from Abdul-Hameed from al-Waleed b. Sabeeh from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Two rakat Salaat of a married person is equal to seventy rakats of an unmarried person.”
